title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is classifying, up to isomorphism, (semi-)simplicial modules L. of finite type over a principal ideal domain k (the ∂-perfect case). Via Dold–Puppe (Dold–Kan) he reduces this to chain complexes of f.g. projective, hence free, k-modules. The previous page splits such a complex as a direct sum of two-term complexes K_i: P_i ↪ Q_i in degrees i and i−1, with P_i ≅ B_{i−1} and Q_i ≅ Z_{i−1}, so that Q_i/P_i ≅ H_{i−1}.

This page refines each K_i in two steps.

(1) Split off the free part of homology. Let P̄_i ⊂ Q_i be the inverse image of the torsion submodule of Q_i/P_i ≅ H_{i−1}. Then N_{i−1} := Q_i/P̄_i ≅ H_{i−1}/torsion is f.g. and torsion-free, hence projective. So Q_i ≅ P̄_i ⊕ N_{i−1}, and K_i ≅ K̄_i ⊕ N_{i−1}[i−1], where K̄_i = (P_i ↪ P̄_i).

(2) Diagonalise the torsion part. P_i ⊂ P̄_i is an inclusion of f.g. projectives of equal rank whose quotient tors H_{i−1} is torsion. By elementary divisors (Smith normal form; this needs k principal), K̄_i is a direct sum of rank-one complexes k --n_{iα}--> k, for 1 ≤ α ≤ rk P_i = rk P̄_i. The n_{iα} ∈ k∖0 are determined up to units once they are chosen increasing for divisibility.

- The n_{iα} that are units give contractible pieces. Under Dold–Kan, k --id--> k in degrees i, i−1 corresponds to a simplicial module of rank C(n,i)+C(n,i−1) = C(n+1,i) in degree n, whence the 'Λ^i' Hilbert function on the next page.
- The non-unit n_{iα} are the invariant factors of tors H_{i−1}.
- The count of each divisor class gives the multiplicities ρ_{i,ℓ}, and the free rank gives ν.

This proves the uniqueness/structure statement announced on the previous page: L. is determined up to isomorphism by the integers μ_i, ν_j, ρ_{i,ℓ}. The next page computes the Hilbert function rk L_n = Σ(μ_i+ρ_i)C(n+1,i) + Σν_j C(n,j), and shows that this function together with the homology data determines L.
errors: Notation slip: the page writes Q_i/B_i ≅ H_{i−1}, but by the previous page's setup it should be Q_i/P_i, with P_i ≅ B_{i−1} ⊂ Q_i ≅ Z_{i−1}. Likewise P̄_i is the inverse image in Q_i, not 'dans B_i'.
Indexing inconsistencies: the free summand is written both N_{i−1} (degree i−1) and 'N_i[−i]'. N_i is also reused for the rank rk P_i, clashing with the module N_{i−1}.

Elementary divisors and freeness require k principal (added as an afterthought). Over a Dedekind ring one would need Steinitz classes as well. The previous page's claim that submodules of f.g. projectives are free is only valid for a PID.

ideas.what: Reduction of simplicial modules of finite type to chain complexes of f.g. projectives via Dold–Puppe
ideas.where_published: Used implicitly in SGA/Illusie's cotangent complex context; not specifically by G.

ideas.what: Splitting a two-term complex of free modules over a PID into a free-homology summand plus a torsion part, diagonalised by Smith normal form
ideas.modern_name: Structure theorem for complexes of free modules over a PID (elementary divisors / Smith normal form)

ideas.what: Complete isomorphism invariants of simplicial free modules over a PID: ranks of contractible blocks, free homology ranks, torsion invariant factors; with the Hilbert function rk L_n as a combination of binomials (continued on next page)
ideas.modern_name: Classification of finite-type simplicial modules over a PID; Dold–Kan rank formula

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine (if carefully executed) step: splitting off free homology and applying Smith normal form to classify complexes of free modules over a PID, as a lemma towards classifying ∂-perfect simplicial modules. It is standard, and nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: '[-l'image-] l'image inverse dans B_i' – the meaning (and likely the intended text) is the inverse image in Q_i; '⊂ Q_i' is written above P̄_i.
'N_{i-1} = Q_i/P̄_i' is written with a corrected subscript; the marginal note reads 'H_{i−1}/torsion' with an ≃ sign, as transcribed.

'les nombres des n_{iα} [?] qui sont[?]' likely reads 'le nombre des n_{iα} qui sont inversibles' (the units, giving contractible pieces). The following line 'est lié à ...' seems to read 'est μ_i (il leur correspond la fonction (Λ^iL)…)', i.e. the Λ^i Hilbert function, not '(Λ̂L)^{H_i}'.
'(n_{iα} bien déterminés à des unités près)' – the second '[?] à des' is likely 'à des unités près' (repeated/struck).
'on prend les n_{i,α} tels qu'ils soient croissants pour la divisibilité, on trouve une suite unique; les multiplicités d'occurrence des diviseurs dans cet ensemble…' continues onto the next page.
